summary: The bill amends NEPA to speed up federal project approvals by narrowing the scope of environmental reviews to only proximate effects, allowing agencies to rely on other statutes or prior state/tribal reviews instead of new analysis, imposing tight deadlines for applications and decisions, limiting judicial review to 150 days with agency deference and no vacatur, and making completed reviews and permits harder to revoke.

scores.thoughts: The bill reforms NEPA permitting processes to expedite economic development projects but contains no provisions that alter federal spending levels, appropriations, or budget authority. It is procedural in nature and has no bearing on government spending.
The bill makes no reference to tax policy, rates, credits, or revenue measures of any kind.
The bill addresses environmental review procedures under NEPA and has no connection to healthcare policy, coverage, or markets.
The bill contains no provisions related to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill does not address immigration, border policy, visas, or enforcement.
The bill has no provisions concerning reproductive rights or abortion access.
While NEPA applies to some defense projects, the bill does not change defense spending levels or military policy.

The bill substantially amends NEPA to narrow the scope of environmental reviews, impose strict deadlines, limit consideration of indirect or cumulative effects, restrict judicial review, and facilitate faster project approvals. These changes are designed to reduce regulatory burdens and expedite development, directly limiting the reach of environmental regulations.
The bill does not address welfare programs, entitlements, or social safety net policies.
The bill contains no provisions related to schools, education funding, or school choice.
The bill has no connection to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance policy.
The bill does not address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
The bill makes no changes to tariffs, trade agreements, or trade regulation.
The bill has no direct provisions affecting deficits, debt ceilings, or fiscal policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
The bill does not address foreign assistance or international aid programs.
The bill has no provisions concerning voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
The bill does not regulate technology companies, data privacy, or digital oversight.
The bill makes no changes to labor law, union rights, or worker protections.
The bill contains no provisions addressing religious exemptions or anti-discrimination law.
